When you define it, it creates an entry in the jacobian dictionary that is an r x c arrary of zeros, and it performs a matrix vector product when derivatives are computed because it sees 0,0 as just another number that needs to be multiplied. This includes:
`time` - The time variable for the entire problem (generally starts at 0 at the beginning of the first phase)
`time_phase` - The elapsed time in the current phase
`states:<state_name}` - Integrated state variables
`controls:<control_name>` - Dynamic control variables
`control_rates:<control_name>_rate[2]` - Dynamic control rate (or second derivative if suffix is `rate2`.
`polynomial_controls:<control_name>` - Controls modeled by a polynomial across the entire phase
`polynomial_control_rates:<control_name>_rate[2] - Time derivatives of the polynomial controls
`parameters:<foo>` - Static parameters in the phase.
`<foo>` - Any ODE output that the user explicitly adds to the timeseries.
